title: Regional playing, the Harlem Country Club and summer layoffs
summary: The band stays regional, playing East St. Louis' Harlem Country Club and country clubs, with its first trips to Cincinnati and the Chicago Savoy in 1937-38.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: : Where did -- where did the band go on tour during this time?
During that time the band just played around small places around here. The band didn't venture out on a tour --
We didn't go back east I know.
Until 19 -- 1938. We took the band to Cincinnati. Remember?
That was the first time we really ventured out. Then one year we went to Chicago, and played the Savoy Ballroom, what year was that, Charles?
That was in '38, no that was in '37, wasn't it?
IN '37. That was a little bit later. Most of our playing, at that time, was regional, you know, we
played East St. Louis. We opened up a place in East St. Louis, called Harlem Country Club, remember Harlem Country Club?
Over in Brooklyn, Illinois. And we played over there every -- every weekend. Every Saturday and every Sunday.
In fact, the guys weren't really too particular, after working those eight months, every night --

Every night. And they actually wanted a vacation, they really wanted (unintelligible), May, June, July and August, four months. Sometime we just played in Alton, right near, it's near -- it's in metropolitan St. Louis. And you get two-three gigs a week, something like that.
We played a -- countryclub dates, you know, and then we started rehearsing again for the next show.
The band was really in demand.
So the band was quite popular here.
